entities.name: Eldrazi
entities.description: Titanic, Ætheric monstrosities native to the spaces between planes, who consume planes from the outside and are trapped on Zendikar.

entities.name: Zendikar
entities.description: A plane threatened by the world-eating Eldrazi and home to adventurers; its setting was crucial to the naming of the Eldrazi.

entities.name: Blind Eternities
entities.description: The spaces between planes, whose nature is incomprehensible to the point of madness and which are the native home of the Eldrazi.

entities.name: The Mending
entities.description: An event that affected the nature of the planeswalker spark.

entities.name: Planeswalkers
entities.description: Beings with a spark who travel between planes and are the protagonists of Magic.

entities.name: Sorin Markov
entities.description: A planeswalker depicted on the Rise of the Eldrazi packaging art.

entities.name: Nissa Revane
entities.description: A planeswalker depicted on the Rise of the Eldrazi packaging art.

entities.name: Akroma
entities.description: A figure whose presence makes a changeling uneasy, used as a joke comparison.

entities.name: Alara
entities.description: A plane covered by the Planeswalker's Guide to Alara and the setting of the Alara Reborn novel.

events.summary: Answering a reader, the author reasons that the Eldrazi, outside their physical forms, would be incomprehensibly powerful in the Blind Eternities.
events.quote: I think the Eldrazi's Ætheric nature, like the Blind Eternities themselves, would be incomprehensible to the point of madness.

events.summary: The author guesses that the Mending did little to the Eldrazi, who have no sparks and are native to the spaces between worlds.
events.quote: They don't have planeswalker sparks, and they don't planeswalk from world to world the way planeswalkers do.

relations.note: The Eldrazi are native to the spaces between worlds.
relations.quote: They are native to the spaces between worlds
